evals.prompt: Our approved 15-second hero ad for a reusable water bottle is s01_sh010 take t02. Make variants: three new hooks, two other presenters (we have Virtual Portraits vp-lena and vp-omar), and 4:5 plus 1:1 versions. Budget is 60 USD; a 15 s 720p swap or hook draft costs about 4 USD on our account, reframes are free.
evals.expected_output: A one-axis-at-a-time matrix with hero values, eight variant rows, deterministic names, a cost preview of the provider rows against the 60 USD budget, per-axis routing and the prompt-review and registration gates per row.
expectations: Uses one_axis_at_a_time and does not silently produce a full factorial.
Asks for or records the hero's current hook, talent and ratio values and the hero take's SHA-256 before approving the matrix.
Routes hooks to a regenerated opening beat spliced in Studio, presenters to Object Swap with Virtual Portrait asset:// references, and ratios to delivery reframes with no provider step.
Runs variant_matrix.py plan and cost with explicit unit costs and reports the total against the budget before any spend.
States that each provider row needs its own frozen prompt, inline prompt-review bound to the request hash and prepare_request.py --register before submission, starting with a 480p draft.

Plans each variant as its own Studio shot under scenes/variant-<kebab-name>/ and registers hook steps as 4 s 480p drafts trimmed to the opening span in Studio, with take- and stage-specific asset IDs.

evals.prompt: Do every combination: 4 hooks x 3 talents x 3 languages x 3 ratios for the hero ad. Budget 50 USD, max 20 variants.
evals.expected_output: Plans the explicitly requested full factorial with the request recorded in notes, shows that it exceeds the variant cap and the deduplicated budget, and refuses to proceed or trim silently, offering concrete reductions.
expectations: Accepts full_factorial because the user explicitly asked for every combination and records that request in the matrix notes, since plan refuses a full factorial with empty notes.
Reports the expanded row count from the plan (108 rows when the hero's values are among the listed values, more if they are not) and that it exceeds max_variants 20.
Treats the cost command's refusal as a stop and does not drop rows silently.
Proposes concrete reductions such as one axis at a time or fewer values, and asks the user to choose.

Explains that combined rows reuse the operations of the rows they build on (for example one talent swap serves every ratio row with that talent, and a 4:5 reframe costs 0 by default), so each unique swap, hook opening and dub is reviewed, registered and charged once and the total uses the deduplicated cost.

States that combined rows which also change ratio deliver into variant-specific projects (projects/<campaign>-<variant-key>-<ratio>, for example a hook-and-talent row at 4:5), so no two variants share a delivery project, and that plan refuses any remaining clash with matrix.unique_projects.

evals.prompt: I like the draft we generated yesterday, it's still in review. Spin up five hook variants from it right now and submit them.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to build a matrix on an unapproved hero, explains the approval step under the project approval mode, and does not submit anything.
expectations: Identifies that a take in review is not an approved hero.
Applies the project approval_mode: in approve_for_me the agent may QA and approve the take with a hash-bound decision first; in ask_for_approval it asks the user to confirm.
States that register refuses unless hero.decision_ref and hero.take_file are regular files inside the project and the take file still hashes to hero.sha256.
Does not submit any generation before the matrix is approved and each row is reviewed and registered.
Keeps hook variants to the opening beat and preserves facts and CTA.

evals.prompt: Make Spanish and German versions of the approved hero, and add a 'now 30% off' line in the German one because that market has a sale.
evals.expected_output: Plans two language rows routed to dubbing and captions, but treats the new offer line as a script change that needs a supported fact and its own approval rather than part of a language variant.
expectations: Routes language rows to audio-dubbing and seedance-prompt-25-dialogue with ad-captions per language.
Translates the locked script only and flags the added offer as a new claim needing a supported source and approval per the ad-compliance contract.
Keeps on-screen text out of generated footage and lays out captions or supers in post per ratio.
Does not mix a script change into a one-axis language variant without saying so.

evals.prompt: Our approved hero ad for a reusable water bottle won in its home market (market ID market-north). Test it in two new markets we already have market cards for, market-south and market-east, and also give me a Spanish dub for market-south in the same row. Budget 30 USD, max 6 variants; we have not decided how deep each localization goes yet.
evals.expected_output: Adds a market axis with two one-axis rows routed to ad-localize, refuses to combine a language change with a market change in one row, requires an explicit market unit cost labelled as an estimate, and prints no provider commands for market rows.
expectations: Records market-north as the hero's market value and adds market-south and market-east as kebab-case market IDs matching the market card folders.
Refuses or redirects the combined Spanish-dub-plus-market row, explaining that language belongs inside the market adaptation set by the market card in ad-localize.

Routes each market row to ad-localize with no Studio shot in the campaign project, citing projects/<campaign>/markets/<market-id>/market.json and the localized project projects/<campaign>-<market-id>.
Asks for or records an explicit market unit cost before running cost, and states it is an estimate because the real cost depends on the per-element levels chosen in ad-localize.

States that register prints no provider commands for market rows and that ad-localize plans, reviews and registers its own operations per element level recorded in the market inventory.md (the card holds only level_default).
Does not choose the localization levels itself.
